name: Thermodynamics
boundaries: Thermodynamics: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: Added as THR-11. It overlaps THR-01 and is not the same concept. THR-01 is a computable closure for turbulent transport. THR-11 is operational state variables for driven matter.

original_dispositions.original_title: one thermodynamic uncertainty relation for every observable and every dynamics
original_dispositions.reason: The classical relation is already a substantial principle, and it is not universal. Maity and Ghoshal find that non-Markovian collisional models violate the classical bound, with the “degree and type of non-Markovianity” affecting the violation. A still tighter relation would be an incremental theorem. Engine consequences of the known tradeoff sit with THR-02.

original_dispositions.original_title: a complete strong-coupling, memory-bearing fluctuation framework
original_dispositions.reason: Pieces exist, including Zambon and Adesso on non-Markovian work extraction. The direct product of a finished formalism is consistent accounting. Provable quantum-machine advantage remains THR-05. Treating the formalism as already revolutionary would count downstream devices that still require that separate breakthrough.

original_dispositions.original_title: a thermodynamic theory of active matter
original_dispositions.reason: Motility-induced phase separation and flocking already have dynamical theories. Bebon, Robinson, and Speck and Gaspard track dissipation for specific active models. The missing state-variable principle is THR-11. A separate entry would duplicate that gap and would inflate pattern-forming materials into a consequence that still needs materials design.

original_dispositions.original_title: an arrow of time from microscopic reversibility with no special initial condition
original_dispositions.reason: The standard statistical account uses a low-entropy initial macrostate and a typical microstate inside it. Arrighi and coauthors prove an entropic arrow “without relying on the past hypothesis” only inside an expanding graph toy model. That does not derive the cosmological arrow from reversible microscopic laws alone. The historical demand is narrower than the open scientific problem and is partly ill-posed.

Shiraishi, Saito, and Tasaki and Pietzonka and Seifert already prove class-dependent tradeoffs. An exact maximum that is independent of the working substance is not established as a well-posed target. The revolutionary capability is the engine that is efficient, powerful, and steady.

Added as THR-12. Rao and Esposito and Liang, De Los Rios, and Busiello show that balances and concentration bounds already exist. The addition is the unmet design step, and it is flagged as overlapping THR-09.

original_dispositions.original_title: potentials for long-range interactions and broken ergodicity, covering glasses, plasmas, gravity, and spin glasses
original_dispositions.reason: The bundle does not name one missing capability. Continuum potentials are THR-01. Operational entropy beyond local equilibrium is THR-11. Horizon temperature is THR-10. A glass-specific resolution of the Kauzmann problem would be an important condensed-matter result. The sources read in this pass did not show that result unlocking a capability of the calibration scale, and this pass did not re-review the primary glass literature.

original_dispositions.original_title: relativistic and gravitational thermodynamic consistency, including the information paradox
original_dispositions.reason: Not added beyond THR-10. A laboratory Unruh temperature is the thermodynamic measurement in that neighborhood. Closing the black-hole information paradox is principally quantum gravity. Counting it here would assign a cross-field problem to thermodynamics.

original_dispositions.original_title: a stable macroscopic negative temperature in a system with an unbounded energy spectrum
original_dispositions.reason: Population inversion as a maximum-entropy state uses an upper bound on energy. Dunkel and Hilbert argue from the Gibbs entropy that absolute temperature remains positive even for bounded spectra. Either reading makes an unbounded-spectrum negative-temperature equilibrium the wrong target: one side treats the upper bound as essential, and the other disputes the thermodynamic interpretation of the existing experiments.
